verdict.rationale: Kong documents its own declarative configuration surfaces. decK is described as a tool for API lifecycle automation (APIOps), Kong supports declarative DB-less deployment, and official Terraform providers manage Gateway entities and Konnect resources, so the declarative, infrastructure-as-code part of the story is clearly met. The evidence only implies the CI-driven sync part through decK's 'automate' framing and never documents a CI pipeline, drift diffing, or a sync workflow, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: explicit documentation of syncing or applying declarative config from CI pipelines (e.g. deck sync/diff in CI), drift detection, independent or hands-on corroboration of a GitOps workflow.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can manage API infrastructure as declarative config and sync it from CI (GitOps/APIOps)

citations.quote: decK is a command line tool that facilitates API Lifecycle Automation (APIOps) by offering a comprehensive toolkit of commands designed to orchestrate and automate
Sophisticated deployment models like Declarative Databaseless Deployment
all configurable via a RESTful admin API or declarative configuration
Designed for use with Kong Gateway on-prem, the `kong-gateway` provider allows you to manage Kong Entities using Terraform
